1.explanation: The accessibility violation comes from FileUploaderDropContainer’s JSX, where a <div role="button"> wraps an <input> element. This nesting of interactive controls triggers WCAG 4.1.2 (“nested-interactive”) errors in axe-core ≥4.2.0. To resolve the issue, the FileUploaderDropContainer function component must be modified—either by removing or relocating the role="button" attribute or by restructuring the markup so that the input is not a descendant of another interactive element.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a newly added axe-core test for FileUploaderDropContainer failing under jest. The failure points to a nested-interactive violation: the component renders a <div role="button"> containing an <input type="file">, which axe-core 4.2.0 flags as nesting interactive controls. Additional images show the test definition in FileUploaderDropContainer-test.js and the updated package.json requiring axe-core ^4.2.0.

2.explanation:
1. FileUploaderDropContainer.js – The function component FileUploaderDropContainer renders a <div role="button"> that contains an <input> element, resulting in nested interactive controls. This markup needs to be refactored to remove the nested role or move the input out of the button container.

2. FileUploaderDropContainer-test.js – A new test case it('should have no axe violations') must be added to this file (or existing tests updated) to include an axe accessibility check. Without this, the nested-interactive violation will go unnoticed in the test suite.
2.bug_scenario: The FileUploaderDropContainer component renders a <div> with role="button" that wraps an <input type="file"/>, causing nested interactive controls and triggering an axe-core nested-interactive violation. The accompanying Jest tests for FileUploaderDropContainer do not include an accessibility (axe) test to catch this, and the project’s axe-core dependency is pinned below the version that reports this violation.
